1.6a — Animation States: IsWalking, WalkDir, Attack

Your player already walks. It does not look alive. Today: the Animator window, four parameters, and the moment you realize animation is the first state machine you ever build — you just get to see this one.

Predict First ~10 min

Until now, our player has been animating a walk cycle constantly from Start(), even when standing completely still. Today, you write UpdateAnimation() in PlayerController.cs to make the animation respond directly to player movement:

bool isMoving = xDirection != 0 || yDirection != 0;
anim.SetBool("IsWalking", isMoving);

if (isMoving)
{
    if (Mathf.Abs(xDirection) >= Mathf.Abs(yDirection))
    {
        anim.SetInteger("WalkDir", 1); // Side
        sprite.flipX = xDirection > 0;
    }
    else
    {
        if (yDirection > 0)
        {
            anim.SetInteger("WalkDir", 0); // Up
            sprite.flipX = true;
        }
        else
        {
            anim.SetInteger("WalkDir", 2); // Down
            sprite.flipX = false;
        }
    }
}

if (Input.GetMouseButtonDown(0))
{
    anim.SetTrigger("Attack");
}

Predict: the code sets four things on the Animator — IsWalking (bool), WalkDir (int: 0 up, 1 side, 2 down), Attack (trigger) — and the sprite's flipX. Draw the four cases (standing / walking left-right / walking up / walking down) and what the animator should show for each. Check yourself against the game after the lab.

Socratic

The code never says "play the walk frames." It only sets state — IsWalking true, WalkDir 2 — and something else decides what animation to run. Where is that decision actually made, and why is splitting it out like this the same idea as the StatManager being separate from the player?

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — open the Animator. Select the Player in the Overworld scene, then Window → Animation → Animator. The player's Animator Controller opens: boxes (states) connected by arrows (transitions). Find the PlayerAnimator child in the Hierarchy — the animator lives on the child, which is why the code says GetComponentInChildren<Animator>().

Step 2 — read the conditions. Click the arrow from the side-walk state to the idle state and read the Inspector: "Exit when IsWalking is false." Click the transitions between up/side/down: they fire on WalkDir equals 0 / 1 / 2. The parameters tab (left of the window) lists all three. That is the whole contract: code sets parameters, the Animator reads them.

Step 3 — the axe variant. The Player prefab ships with animation variants including one holding an axe. Find the axe-walk state(s) in the animator. Nothing points at them yet — you will wire hasAxe into this machine in 5.1a. Today: just find it, and leave a comment in your fork's README about which state names exist.

Bug Hunt: Break the walk cycle

Break each one in the Animator window, run the game, describe what you see, then fix it:

  1. Set the side→idle transition's condition to "IsWalking is true." What does walking do now, and why?
  2. Delete the WalkDir condition from the up/side transition. What happens when you walk diagonally up-right — and why did the code's >= matter?
  3. In the code, comment out the sprite.flipX line. Which direction can you never face, and what exactly did flipX do?
  4. Set the Attack trigger from the code — click the mouse. The trigger fires once per click: what would break if the code used SetBool instead of SetTrigger?
Tinker ~10 min

Tinker: Your animation state diagram

  1. On paper, draw every state the Player animator can be in, with arrows and the parameter conditions on each arrow. How many states does the shipped animator have, and can every state reach every other one?
  2. Write your own C# one-liner that makes the player look attacked: where would you put a Hurt trigger if the boss unit needed one?

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Open the Animator window and read transitions + conditions
  • Explain SetBool vs SetInteger vs SetTrigger with the player's parameters as examples
  • Explain the code↔Animator split: code sets state, Animator plays frames
  • Draw the player's animation state diagram from memory
